learningObjectives: Use Agile Workbench to manage user stories, bugs, and feedback items across features and releases.
Describe CI/CD pipelines, Deployment Manager, and agile development best practices in Pega Platform.

elements.description: Two AI-assisted development tools in App Studio:
items: Application profile: up-to-date view of all work items, features, and status
Developer Assistant pane: AI-powered aids with 4 tabs — Guidance, Knowledge, Work, Checklists

elements.description: Features = capabilities the application supports. Subfeatures = features nested within a feature. When you create a new Case Type, Pega automatically creates a feature with the same name. Work items are associated with features or subfeatures.
Work items tracked in the Application profile:
items: Stories (User stories): describe business requirements; make up the majority of development work; can be uploaded from Excel in bulk
Bugs: document feature defects; major bugs are addressed before minor ones
Feedback items: enhancement requests identified during playback sessions

elements.term: Work item status — drag to change
elements.description: Work item status options: To do → Doing → Done. Change status by DRAGGING the card to the appropriate column on the Kanban board — not by editing a form field.

Integrates with Agile Studio (expanded functionality: release management, progress tracking, team capacity, analytics). Also integrates with external tools: Jira, CA Agile Central — allowing customers to use their existing infrastructure.

elements.text: CI/CD is like a car assembly line with quality checkpoints. CI is the early part: workers (developers) frequently add parts (code changes), robots (automated tests) check each part before it moves forward. If a part fails inspection, the line STOPS. CD is the downstream line: the car is tested at speed, compatibility, and safety gates before reaching the customer (production). Deployment Manager is the factory floor supervisor who orchestrates the whole line automatically.

elements.description: A collaborative practice between development, quality, and operations:
items: Goal: deliver high-quality software in an automated, agile way
Reduces time to market without compromising quality
CI/CD pipeline = the automated process from development through testing to deployment

elements.description: Developers frequently check in changes. Automated build verifies each change — identifies issues EARLY. 'Ready to share' step: new changes work with existing app. 'Integrate changes' step: critical tests pass → changes published to development repository.
The deployment pipeline stages after CI:
items: Rigorous automated regression testing
Changes deployed to staging for further testing
'Ready to accept': acceptance criteria tests pass
'Ready to deploy': performance and compatibility tests pass
Deploy: validates in preproduction → production → post-deployment tests with rollback option
Accessed in ADMIN STUDIO (not App Studio or Dev Studio)
Automates CI/CD workflows: branch merging, application packaging, promoting to environments
Eliminates manual admin promotion
Supports third-party integration: Jenkins, Microsoft Azure DevOps

elements.description: ① Real-time updates: frequent small-scope development iterations. ② Testing: continuous validation to identify and address issues early. ③ Branches: concurrent team development environment to maximize productivity.
Best practices for Continuous Integration in Pega:
items: Test early and often: run Pega unit tests + critical integration tests before packaging
If tests fail → STOP the release pipeline until fixed
Automate: trigger merges and builds via Deployment Manager
Update Rules: keep product Ruleset versions current

elements.description: ① Create test environments (Docker/UAT). ② Run regression tests — UI and service layer. ③ Use version control: target specific Ruleset versions for production. ④ Define a rollback strategy. ⑤ Annotate passing packages as deployment-ready.

examPitfalls.title: Deployment Manager is in Admin Studio — not Dev Studio or App Studio
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where to access Deployment Manager. Candidates select Dev Studio (deployments are development activities) or App Studio (Agile Workbench is there). Deployment Manager lives in Admin Studio.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Deployment Manager is accessed in ADMIN STUDIO. It is not found in App Studio or Dev Studio.

examPitfalls.title: New Case Type auto-creates a feature with the same name
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks what a developer must do after creating a new Case Type to track it in Agile Workbench. Candidates describe manually creating a Feature — not knowing Pega auto-creates one with the same name.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When you create a new Case Type, Pega automatically creates a feature with the same name in Agile Workbench.

examPitfalls.title: 3 work item types — Feedback ≠ Bug
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question presents four types — Story, Bug, Feedback, Task — and asks which three are valid. Candidates remove Task. Correct answer: remove Feedback... wait, the 3 types ARE Story, Bug, Feedback. Candidates remove Feedback thinking it's not a formal type.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Stories = business requirements. Bugs = feature defects. Feedback items = enhancement requests from playback sessions. These are three distinct types.

examPitfalls.title: CI test failure STOPS the pipeline — do not continue
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A scenario describes a CI pipeline where one test fails. Candidates say 'CI marks it failed but packages and delivers anyway.' CI hard-stops on failure — nothing is packaged or delivered until tests pass.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If tests fail during CI, STOP the release pipeline until the issue is fixed. Do not allow failing changes to proceed.

examPitfalls.title: Change work item status by DRAGGING the card — not editing a form
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask how an SA updates a work item from 'To Do' to 'Doing.' Candidates describe opening the item and editing a Status field. The correct method is to drag the card to the target column on the Kanban board.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In Agile Workbench, status is changed by DRAGGING the card to the appropriate column (To do, Doing, Done). It's a Kanban-style board.

examPitfalls.title: CD rollback strategy: if test fails → roll back latest import
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A CD best-practices question asks the correct response to a failed deployment test. Candidates describe retrying or debugging in production. The documented strategy is immediate rollback of the latest import.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If a test fails during CD → roll back the latest import. If all tests pass → annotate the package as ready to deploy.

examPitfalls.title: Agile Studio EXPANDS Agile Workbench — they are not the same tool
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask whether Agile Studio and Agile Workbench are the same. Candidates say yes because both handle work items. Agile Studio is a separate product with release management and progress tracking — Agile Workbench is a component of it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Agile Studio is a SEPARATE tool that expands Agile Workbench with: release management, progress tracking, team capacity, and analytics.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The Developer Assistant pane in Agile Workbench has four tabs. Which set correctly identifies all four?

options.text: Guidance, Knowledge, Work, Checklists
Stories, Bugs, Feedback, Checklists
Features, Subfeatures, Work Items, Releases
Guidance, Tasks, Bugs, Releases

practiceQuiz.hint: The Developer Assistant pane provides AI-powered coding and configuration suggestions to developers.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Developer Assistant pane has four AI-powered tabs: Guidance, Knowledge, Work, and Checklists. It is accessed from the pane area in App Studio and Dev Studio to support developers during configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What happens automatically in Agile Workbench when a developer creates a new Case Type?

options.text: A feature with the same name as the Case Type is automatically created
A user story describing the Case Type is automatically generated
A subfeature is created under the first existing feature
A bug tracking entry is created for the Case Type

practiceQuiz.hint: In Agile Workbench, Case Types map directly to features and epics automatically.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When you create a new Case Type in App Studio, Pega automatically creates a corresponding Feature with the same name in Agile Workbench — no manual Agile Workbench step is required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During a playback session, a business stakeholder identifies an enhancement they want in a future release. Which work item type should the developer create?

options.text: Feedback item
Bug
User story
Subfeature

practiceQuiz.hint: Enhancement requests from playback sessions have a specific work item type.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Feedback items (enhancement requests from playback sessions), Bugs (defects), and User stories (business requirements) are three distinct artifact types in Agile Workbench — each has a different purpose and is tracked separately.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you change the status of a work item from 'To do' to 'Doing' in Agile Workbench?

options.text: Drag the card to the Doing column
Edit the work item form and update the Status field
Right-click the card and select Change Status
Use the Developer Assistant pane to update status

practiceQuiz.hint: Agile Workbench organizes user stories and bugs on a Kanban-style board view.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Status is changed by dragging the card to the appropriate column (To do, Doing, Done) — it is a Kanban board, not a form edit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega System Architect needs to configure and monitor a CI/CD pipeline to automate the promotion of application changes from the Development environment to the Test environment. Where is the Deployment Manager tool accessed in Pega Platform?

options.text: Admin Studio
App Studio
Dev Studio
Agile Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: It's in the studio focused on platform administration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Deployment Manager, Pega's CI/CD orchestration tool, is accessed through Admin Studio — not App Studio or Dev Studio. From Admin Studio, teams design pipeline stages, configure deployment steps, and monitor pipeline runs. A common exam distractor is Dev Studio, which is used for Rule development and is not where CI/CD pipelines are managed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A business stakeholder asks a Pega SA to explain what DevOps means in the context of Pega Platform and how it improves the speed and quality of application delivery compared to traditional siloed development. What is DevOps in the context of Pega Platform?

options.text: A collaborative effort between development, quality, and operations to deliver high-quality software in an automated, agile way
A tool for automating branch merging and application packaging
A methodology that replaces Agile Workbench for release management
A framework that eliminates the need for testing in CI/CD pipelines

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall Pega's definition of DevOps — which three organizational functions does it unite?
practiceQuiz.rationale: DevOps in Pega is a cultural and technical practice that brings together development, quality assurance, and operations teams to shorten the application delivery cycle while maintaining quality. It is broader than any single tool. Deployment Manager is the specific Pega tooling that implements the CI/CD pipeline — it is one artifact of DevOps practice, not its definition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During continuous integration, unit tests fail for newly introduced changes. According to best practices, what should happen?

options.text: Stop the release pipeline until the issue is fixed
Proceed to packaging and fix in the next sprint
Mark the test as a known issue and continue
Move the changes to staging for further testing

practiceQuiz.hint: Failing tests in CI should block further progress.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Best practice: if tests fail during CI, STOP the release pipeline until the issue is fixed. Do not allow failing changes to proceed to packaging or staging.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which step in the continuous delivery pipeline verifies performance, scale, and compatibility tests before production deployment?

options.text: Ready to deploy
Ready to share
Integrate changes
Ready to accept

practiceQuiz.hint: This step comes just before the actual production deploy.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The 'Ready to deploy' step verifies performance, scale, and compatibility tests. 'Ready to accept' tests acceptance criteria. 'Ready to share' and 'Integrate changes' are CI steps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does Deployment Manager help eliminate manual work in a DevOps workflow?

options.text: It automates Branch merging, application packaging, and promoting the application to different environments
It automatically writes user stories based on application configuration
It replaces the need for third-party DevOps tools entirely
It runs production-level testing on the live environment without human intervention

practiceQuiz.hint: Which three specific tasks does Deployment Manager automate in a Pega DevOps workflow?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Deployment Manager automates Branch merging, application packaging, and environment promotion — eliminating manual admin promotion. It supports (not replaces) third-party tools like Jenkins and Azure DevOps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO third-party DevOps tools does Pega Platform's Deployment Manager support for open DevOps integration?

options.text: Jenkins
Microsoft Azure DevOps
Jira
GitHub Actions

practiceQuiz.hint: Jira integrates with Agile Workbench, not the DevOps pipeline.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Deployment Manager integrates with Jenkins and Microsoft Azure DevOps for CI/CD. Jira integrates with Agile Workbench for work item tracking — it is not a DevOps pipeline tool.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test fails during the continuous delivery stage. What is the recommended action?

options.text: Roll back the latest import
Annotate the package as partially tested and continue
Skip the failing test and move to production
Create a feedback item and deploy anyway

practiceQuiz.hint: CD best practices include defining a rollback strategy in case tests fail post-deployment.
practiceQuiz.rationale: In Pega's Continuous Delivery pipeline, the outcome of automated tests determines the next action. If any test in the pipeline fails, the team must roll back the latest import to restore the stable state. If all tests pass, the deployment package is annotated as ready to deploy, clearing it for promotion to the next environment or to production.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer asks an SA about the relationship between Agile Studio and Agile Workbench when deciding how to track user stories and log bugs during an upcoming sprint in a Pega project. How does Agile Studio relate to Agile Workbench in Pega Platform?

options.text: Agile Studio is a separate Pega tool that expands Agile Workbench with release management, progress tracking, team capacity, and analytics
Agile Studio and Agile Workbench are the same tool with different names
Agile Studio is a simplified version of Agile Workbench for business analysts
Agile Studio replaces Agile Workbench in Pega Platform v8

practiceQuiz.hint: One expands the other with more robust capabilities.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Agile Workbench is the built-in Pega tool for creating and managing user stories, bugs, and feedback. It integrates directly with the Case Type structure without requiring an external tool.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is using Pega Agile Workbench to manage development work. Which TWO work item types can be created and tracked in Agile Workbench?

options.text: User Stories — describing a feature or capability from the end-user's perspective
Bugs — tracking defects identified during development, testing, or user acceptance
Sprint velocity reports — automatically generated productivity metrics from team commit activity

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega team is implementing CI/CD pipelines for a new Pega application. Which TWO statements correctly describe CI/CD pipeline behavior in Pega Platform?

options.text: A CI/CD pipeline automates the build, test, and deployment of Pega application changes across multiple environments
Pega Deployment Manager orchestrates the pipeline, coordinating automated tests and environment promotions
CI/CD pipelines in Pega always require a manual approval gate at every environment and cannot be fully automated
CI/CD pipelines in Pega replace all Ruleset versioning, eliminating the need for Branch Rulesets

practiceQuiz.hint: CI/CD automates build-test-deploy across environments; Deployment Manager is the orchestration tool.
practiceQuiz.rationale: CI/CD pipelines in Pega automate the process of building, running automated tests, and promoting application changes through environments. Pega Deployment Manager is the orchestration layer that manages pipeline stages and integrations. Pipelines can be configured for fully automated promotion without mandatory manual gates, and Branch Rulesets remain part of development management alongside CI/CD.
